sources: SemVer 2.0.0 precedence rules, https://semver.org/#spec-item-11 (numeric components, pre-release lower than release, build metadata ignored)
RFC 3339 section 5.6 date-time, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339#section-5.6 (lower-case t and z allowed, offset required)

defects.class: string comparison of numeric version components
defects.description: Quoted line: core_parts = tuple(self.core.split(".")). Components stay strings, so the tuple compares lexically. Input compare_versions("1.10.0", "1.9.0") returns -1 (wrong; expected 1 under R1). Base code returns 1. Downstream: code/release_check.py require_newer(ledger 1.10.0, published 1.9.0) raises ReleaseCheckError "1.10.0 must be higher than 1.9.0"; the release gate blocks a valid release.

Quoted line: return core_parts + (0, ()). A release gets sort slot 0 and a pre-release gets slot 1, so the release sorts below its pre-release. Input compare_versions("1.0.0", "1.0.0-rc1") returns -1 (wrong; expected 1 under R2). compare_versions("1.0.0-rc1", "1.0.0") returns 1 (wrong; expected -1). Evidence: printed values from build_h4.py run against code/.

defects.class: case-sensitive RFC 3339 delimiter and offset designator
defects.description: Quoted line: the _TIMESTAMP_PATTERN regex literal with literal T and Z. Input '2026-10-15t08:00:00z' raises TimestampError (not an RFC 3339 timestamp). Under R4 it is valid and equals 2026-10-15 08:00:00+00:00. Cross-file trace: code/manifest.py _entry_from_dict calls parse_timestamp on released_at; a manifest written in lower case by another tool, e.g. {"component":"ledger","version":"1.0.0","released_at":"2026-10-15t08:00:00z"}, makes load_manifest raise ManifestError "entry 0 is invalid: not an RFC 3339 timestamp". Evidence: printed values from build_h4.py run against code/.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Quoted line: return Version(raw=stripped, pre=match.group(4), build=match.group(5)). Build metadata is stored but precedence_key uses only core and pre, so R3 holds. compare_versions("1.0.0+build.7", "1.0.0") returns 0, which is correct.

Quoted line: return candidate_major > previous_major. MAJOR is converted with int() before comparison, so it is numeric, the same pattern as D1 done correctly. is_major_bump("9.9.9", "10.0.0") returns True, which is correct.

Quoted line: if offset is None:. The regex makes the offset optional, and this check rejects it, so R5 holds. parse_timestamp("2026-10-15T08:00:00") raises TimestampError (timestamp must carry an offset or Z), which is correct.

Quoted line: with open(path, "w") as handle:. Real flaw on an unchanged line: no encoding is given, so the platform default is used. On a cp1252 Windows host, a component name such as "数据" raises UnicodeEncodeError from _write_report, which main does not catch. The change does not touch cli.py and the spec does not cover report encoding, so a diff-mode review must not report it.
